from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Information is measured by narrowing down possibilities.",
            "Surprise equates to the amount of information gained.",
            "Entropy quantifies the average surprise of a result.",
            "Finding rare outcomes yields high information.",
            "Common outcomes provide little new information."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Intuition: What is Information?", lecture_lines)
        
        # Assets (SVGs)
        box_path = "/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/box.svg"
        
        boxes = VGroup(*[SVGMobject(box_path).set_color("#FFD700") for _ in range(5)])
        q_marks = VGroup(*[Text("?", color="#FFD700", font_size=30) for _ in range(5)])
        
        # Assemble boxes
        box_elements = VGroup()
        for i in range(5):
            pair = VGroup(boxes[i], q_marks[i])
            box_elements.add(pair)
            self.place_at_grid(pair, f"B{i+1}", scale_factor=0.6)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(box_elements))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#3498DB")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Using VideoCritic fix for positioning
        self.place_in_area(box_elements, 'B2', 'B4', scale_factor=0.9)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#F1C40F")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Use placeholders for symbols as per storyboard
        symbol_rare = Text("★", color="#00FF00", font_size=40)
        symbol_common = Text("●", color="#FFFFFF", font_size=40)
        
        # VideoCritic fixes for C2, C3
        self.place_at_grid(symbol_rare, 'C2', scale_factor=0.7)
        self.place_at_grid(symbol_common, 'C3', scale_factor=0.7)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(symbol_rare), FadeIn(symbol_common))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#2ECC71")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        high_info_circle = Circle(color="#FF4500").surround(symbol_rare)
        self.play(Create(high_info_circle))
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#E74C3C")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        final_text = Text("Information = Surprise", color=WHITE, font_size=30)
        self.place_in_area(final_text, 'A2', 'C5', scale_factor=0.8) # VideoCritic fix for Grid_Visual_Text
        self.play(FadeOut(VGroup(box_elements, symbol_rare, symbol_common, high_info_circle)), FadeIn(final_text))
        self.lecture[4].set_color("#E67E22")
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Shannon entropy formula defines information uncertainty.",
            "Guesses create partitions of the remaining words.",
            "Entropy measures how evenly we split partitions.",
            "Balanced splits maximize information gain.",
            "Uneven partitions represent low entropy."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Mathematical Foundation: Shannon Entropy", lecture_lines)
        
        # Asset path
        asset_bar = "/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/bar.svg"
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show Shannon Entropy formula: H(X) = -sum(p log p)
        formula = MathTex(r"H(X) = -\sum p(i) \log_2 p(i)", color="#00FF00")
        self.place_at_grid(formula, 'C2', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#00FF00")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Explain variables p (probability) and H (entropy)
        label_h = Text("H = Uncertainty", font_size=20, color="#1E90FF").next_to(formula, DOWN)
        label_p = Text("p = Probability", font_size=20, color="#1E90FF").next_to(label_h, DOWN)
        self.play(Write(label_h), Write(label_p))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#1E90FF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Animate bar chart using [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/bar.svg]
        bar_chart = SVGMobject(asset_bar, color="#ADFF2F")
        self.place_in_area(bar_chart, 'D3', 'F5', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(FadeIn(bar_chart))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#ADFF2F")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Update H value (simulation) as bars change shape
        h_val = Text("H = 4.2", font_size=24, color="#FFD700").next_to(bar_chart, UP)
        self.play(Write(h_val))
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#FFD700")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Highlight the peak of the chart to show max entropy
        self.play(bar_chart.animate.set_color("#FF4500"))
        self.lecture[4].set_color("#FF4500")
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Application: The Game Logic", [
            "Guess, then partition the remaining word set.", 
            "Recalculate entropy for all potential remaining words.", 
            "Select the word with the highest entropy value."
        ])
        
        # Elements
        word_set_box = Square(side_length=1.5, color=WHITE).set_fill(BLUE, opacity=0.3)
        word_set_label = Text("Word Set", font_size=24)
        word_group = VGroup(word_set_box, word_set_label)
        self.place_at_grid(word_group, 'B2', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.add(word_group)

        entropy_gauge = VGroup(
            Rectangle(width=2, height=0.5, color=WHITE),
            Rectangle(width=1.5, height=0.4, color=YELLOW).set_fill(YELLOW, opacity=0.8).align_to(word_set_box, LEFT)
        )
        entropy_label = Text("Entropy", font_size=20)
        entropy_group = VGroup(entropy_gauge, entropy_label).arrange(DOWN)

        # Asset: Wordle Grid
        wordle_grid = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/grid.svg")
        self.place_at_grid(wordle_grid, 'C5', scale_factor=0.8)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#87CEFA")
        partition_lines = VGroup(*[Line(self.grid['B2'], self.grid[target], color=WHITE) for target in ['D2', 'D4', 'D6']])
        self.play(Create(partition_lines), FadeIn(wordle_grid))
        
        guess_text = Text("GUESS", font_size=24, color="#FFD700")
        self.place_at_grid(guess_text, 'B4')
        self.play(Write(guess_text))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFD700")
        self.place_at_grid(entropy_group, 'E3', scale_factor=0.7)
        self.play(FadeIn(entropy_group))
        
        # Visualize entropy check
        check_marker = Dot(color=RED)
        self.place_at_grid(check_marker, 'E5', scale_factor=0.5)
        self.play(Flash(check_marker))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FF6347")
        target_icon = Star(color=GREEN, fill_opacity=1).scale(0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(target_icon, 'E4', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(GrowFromCenter(target_icon))
        self.play(Indicate(target_icon))

outline.topic: Cracking the Code: Information Theory and Entropy in Wordle
outline.target_audience: University students (CS or Data Science focus)

sections.title: The Intuition: What is Information?
sections.content: Introduce the concept of 'surprise' in data. Information is measured by how much a result narrows down the set of possibilities. We define 'Entropy' as the average amount of surprise or uncertainty reduction per guess.
sections.example: Visual: A bag of 100 colored balls (99 white, 1 black). Finding the black ball provides high 'information' (low probability), while finding a white ball provides low 'information'.

sections.title: Mathematical Foundation: Shannon Entropy
sections.content: Define the formula H = -Σ p(i) log2 p(i). Explain that each guess in Wordle creates a 'partition' of possible remaining words. Entropy measures the spread of these partitions; we want a guess that splits the pool as evenly as possible.
sections.example: Visual: A bar graph showing a 'flat' distribution (high entropy/better) vs. a 'spiked' distribution (low entropy/worse) when analyzing the impact of the word 'CRANE'.

sections.title: Strategy: Maximizing Information Gain
sections.content: Apply the theory to Wordle. A 'good' word isn't necessarily one that matches letters, but one that eliminates the largest number of incorrect candidates. Explain the transition from 'Maximum Entropy' (best average case) to 'Minimax' (best worst-case).
sections.example: Scenario: 'CRANE' vs. 'XYLYL'. 'CRANE' eliminates thousands of words regardless of the feedback pattern, whereas 'XYLYL' rarely helps narrow the field.

sections.title: Application: The Game Logic
sections.content: Show the feedback loop: Guess -> Partition remaining word set -> Recalculate entropy for all remaining words -> Pick the highest entropy word. This is how algorithms like 'WordleBot' beat humans.
sections.example: Animated flow: Robot character 'Bit' looks at the list of 2,309 possible words, simulates the 'grey', 'yellow', and 'green' outcomes, and selects the word with the highest entropy value.

sections.title: Summary & Conclusion
sections.content: Reiterate that entropy is a tool for decision-making under uncertainty. Mastery of information theory allows us to turn a game of 'guessing' into a game of 'optimization'.
sections.example: Visual: A 'decision tree' shrinking from thousands of branches down to one single leaf node in just 3-4 steps.
